steps.text: In a medium saucepan over medium heat, combine cocoa, sugar and water. Bring to a boil and let boil 1 minute. Remove from heat and stir in vanilla.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Just cocoa, sugar, water and vanilla in this quick chocolate sauce.
raw_recipe.name: Chocolate Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: In a medium saucepan over medium heat, combine cocoa, sugar and water. Bring to a boil and let boil 1 minute. Remove from heat and stir in vanilla.

review.reviewBody: Very good. I used 2/3 cup milk in place of the water after reading other reviews. Turned out a little thick after it cooled so I stirred in couple TBSP milk to get my desired consistency. 10-18-08: The consistency of the sauce is perfect when I use 1 cup milk in place of the 1 1/4 cups water with out adding extra milk at the end.

Good, basic chocolate sauce. As written, this is a 3 to 4 star. Make it a 5 to 6 star by listening to other reviewers. One cup milk replaces all water. A pinch of salt ups the flavor considerably. Stir in a dab of butter with the vanilla to get a velvety texture. 

NOTES: 1. Use a bigger pot than you think you need! It boils high! 2. This makes a lot! Well over two cups. 3. Stir all lumps out of cocoa prior to making. 4. You don't need syrup to thicken this. That stuff is so bad for you. This is a make ahead recipe that gradually thickens as it cools. 

I'll make this often. So rich! Wonderful over chocolate chip pancakes.

Simple and does the trick. Very versatile recipe for add-ins. Per recommendation, used 1 cup of milk. Used dark cocoa powder which added more depth. Use a whisk to prevent burning and boil over. I played with it by adding a teaspoon of chili powder, cinnamon, and a dash of almond extract in addition to the vanilla. Sure was tasty and perfect over ice cream...or to eat with your fingers...hahaha. Thickens more when it cools.

Tastes great! I think the trick to this is cooking it in a skillet and boiling it for at least 2 minutes. I also followed other reviewers and only used 1 cup of water and added 1 tablespoon of cornstarch. I stirred constantly while cooking and while allowing it to cool a bit. This sauce was the perfect consistency and SOO delicious!

Very good! Most of the bottled chocolate syrups contain high fructose corn syrup and other ingredients we don't bring home.
With this recipe I can use organic products.
This is my second time to use the recipe. My husband likes it in his coffee. 
This time, I started the water boiling while I measured the cocoa and sugar into a bowl. Stirring the sugar and cocoa smoothed the small lumps and it dissolved quickly in the hot water. I added a 1/2 teaspoon of salt with the sugar. And added 1/4 cup coconut oil (butter would be good, also) with the vanilla.
Also, I boiled it for five minutes. 
Expect a thin consistency with a full, rich chocolaty flavor.
--It makes more than two cups of sauce.

My second time making this, with equal success. I did cut the water to one cup, and added about a tablespoon of corn syrup both times (because I had it). I mostly wanted it to add to almond or soy milk and use in coffee, and it's perfect for that.
To anyone saying it was bitter or thin, first, try following the recipe. You do need to stir for a good 10 to 15 minutes at medium heat before it even comes to a boil, and continue for a timed minute after. Take the pot off the hot burner and continue to stir a while, or it will scorch . I didn't add the vanilla until it had cooled a bit, and yes, that does help.
It's just about as thick as the Hersheys sryup, and even though I used a cheap brand of cocoa, I think much better. The type of cocoa you use will make a difference, but mostly, keep stirring, and don't let it scorch.
Favorite but with minor tweak. Used 2/3 c milk and 1/3 c water instead of the 1 1/4 c water. Key for me to get good consistency is to keep heat on medium. Should boil for 1 min while stirring.

Super easy and delicious! I only used 1 cup of water as other comments suggested and it turned out great. Be sure to use a MEDIUM saucepan and not small, since the sauce doubles in size when boiling. Also, be mindful that cocoa powder hates water, so mix it with your sugar before adding the water.

I boiled for about 5-8 minutes for a thicker hot-fudgey sauce. Also, I chose to use water like the recipe calls for instead of using milk (as many people here have done) so that my sauce will keep indefinitely in the refrigerator. I poured the sauce in a glass bottle that used to be for maple syrup - easy to reheat and pour when desired!

BUT I really tweaked it by not using any sugar. I used the 2/3 c. cocoa then used 1/4 c. Stevia. 1/4c fat-free 1/2 & 1/2, 1/4c corn syrup, 1/2 c fat free milk. Added 1 Tbs sweet butter and pinch of cinnamon. Because there was no liquid from the melted sugar I then added water after it boiled and it was perfect. Then vanilla. It could use even less Stevia because it was very rich. I use Trader Joes Baking Cocoa for everything.

Easy to make, but I also changed the liquid to 1/2 C corn syrup, 1/2 C milk & 1/4 C water. It make a good amount of syrup so use a large pan for the boiling. I was concerned about how thin it was, but it thickens after cooling. Allow enough time to cool before you use it.

As with other reviewers, I used 1 cup milk vs. water and added 2 Tbsp. of light corn syrup. However, I also added 1 tsp. of instant coffee granules to deepen the flavor. What a hit -- my family can't get enough of this syrup.
I made this exactly as directed and it's perfect! Unlike other reviewers, I didn't want a thick sauce and specifically wanted a dairy free sauce. This is great for what I wanted it for.
Easy to make and has a very rich chocolate taste but the sauce is too thin for my liking.
I’ve tried my share of these sauce recipes. This one is perfect as is for two reasons - it’s really tasty, and it keeps it’s consistency in the fridge for a long time. Wouldn’t change a thing!
I reduce the amount of sugar.
not bad but i wanted a creamier sauce

Very easy to make and delicious deep-chocolate taste. It reminds me of the Hershey's syrup we used to buy when I was a kid - the consistency and flavor are similar. I gave 4 stars because I would like the consistency to be thicker. This is easy to double or triple if you need a lot. As is, the recipe makes about 8 ounces.
Very good just didn't thicken up that much.
Following others' advice, I used 1/2 c karo and 1/2 c milk + 1/4 c water. I also cut waaay back on the sugar. I used about half the amount called for in the recipe and that was sufficient for me.
